Job Posting: Statewide PBT Monitoring Coordinator



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-527206* 

Statewide PBT Monitoring Coordinator
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)
$7,820\.00 \- $10,732\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/13/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Fisheries Branch is seeking motivated candidates for a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) position. This position serves as the subject matter expert and coordinator for efforts to incorporate Parentage\-Based Tagging (PBT) into existing or new salmonid monitoring programs and anadromous hatchery practices for the purposes of conservation, mitigation and enhancement of California’s salmon fisheries. The incumbent will provide coordination and expertise for developing, implementing and integrating PBT into anadromous hatchery practices, coordinating tissue sampling in recreational and commercial fisheries, escapement, and emigration monitoring surveys. Coordinate with internal programs, and state and federal partners, ensuring that monitoring activities are scientifically sound and aligned with management needs.  

  

  

The position will provide technical expertise to interagency workgroups, participate in evaluating hatchery release strategies and interpret and communicate genetic analyses for application in fisheries and hatchery management. The position oversees the development and management of long term genetic databases, working closely with IT staff and genetic laboratories to establish data sharing agreements and integrate data systems. Responsibilities include conducting data analyses, ensuring data quality, and preparing presentations, technical reports, and annual summaries. The incumbent may also contribute to peer reviewed publications.  

  

  

Candidates should demonstrate strong initiative, professionalism, and the ability to manage complex projects independently. Effective decision making skills, adaptability, and the ability to work productively with interdisciplinary teams and diverse stakeholders are essential. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required, including the ability to convey technical information clearly and professionally.  

  

  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.

• Position is primarily focused on data analyses and management, both of which often require sitting for long periods of time and maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Work several hours in an office setting (both standing and sitting). Work several hours on a computer.
• Typical working hours are 8:00 AM\-5:00 PM Mon\-Fri. Occasional fieldwork and time sensitive projects may require travel outside of normal business hours.
• Occasional travel (up to 10%), including some overnight or multi day travel operating Department vehicles to remote locations when working with hatcheries, in the field, or to present at conferences or workshops.
• Possession of a valid State Driver’s License is required.
• Telework available in compliance with Department policies.

**Final Filing Date:** **8/17/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The incumbent conducts monitoring for the presence of invasive mussels, respond to reports of invasive mussels on waterways, and conducts outreach. Work in this position requires independent application of monitoring protocols and responses to invasive mussels. This position works closely with regional and headquarters staff, external agency staff, and the public.
Conducting monitoring requires following established protocols for eDNA, veliger, and adult mussel sampling. Collect the associated water quality samples and data at mussel monitoring locations using water quality instruments including dissolved Oxygen, pH, temperature, and conductivity. Safely operate and drive a 4x4 State vehicle to reach field sites. Record data and maintain sampling records and results. Complete summaries and reports on sampling efforts and maintain sample Chain of Custody. Be part of a team helping to protect California's natural resources.

Environmental Scientist (Contaminated Land) \- ( 260000JK )


**Description**


We have an exciting opportunity for an **Environmental Scientist** to join our growing **Contaminated Land team** in South Brisbane. In this role, you’ll contribute to a diverse range of projects, delivering high\-quality technical outcomes while playing an important part in the continued growth and success of our broader Geosciences business.


As part of our collaborative Contaminated Land Team, you’ll work alongside industry\-leading experts, including Principal and Senior Scientists and Engineers, who are committed to supporting your professional development. We offer flexibility such as work from home, staggered hours as well as additional Purchased Leave options to balance your career and family life. At Stantec, you’ll be empowered to shape your own career path with access to tailored development opportunities, ongoing training, and the support needed to achieve your long\-term career goals.


**Day to day tasks would involve:**


* Delivery of preliminary and detailed contaminated land assessments, including site management plans, remediation action plans and high\-quality technical reports.
* Plan and carry out field investigations across soil, vapour, surface water and groundwater, including supervising drilling and sampling programs.
* Work alongside technical specialists and subject matter experts, contributing your insights and learning from others.
* Interpret complex datasets and confidently communicate findings through clear, well\-structured and defensible reporting.
* Play an active role in developing proposals, budgets and tenders, directly contributing to the growth and direction of the team.

**To be successful in the role, you’ll need:**


* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Hydrogeology or Geology.
* 3 years’ minimum experience in the contaminated land industry.
* Exposure to a diverse range of contaminated land investigations across different sites, contaminants and project types.
* Sound soil logging, data management, analytical and technical writing skills, with pride in producing high\-quality work.
* A current driver’s licence and willingness to undertake field work.
* We also have interest in hearing from applicants who have experience in one or several of the following areas (although these are not critical):

» water quality assessment (groundwater, surface water, wastewater, irrigation),


» acid sulphate soils and acid mine drainage,


» landfill assessment and management,


» compliance monitoring/reporting


**This position includes both office and field work, and applicants must be physically able to stand and work in the field.**


**What we offer:**


Along with a competitive remuneration package commensurate with skills and experience, we offer a number of benefits to ensure ongoing professional development and well\-being:


* Part of a broader Environment and Geoscience Team with support across Australia, and the opportunity to diversify your skill set nationally and globally.
* Learning and talent development programs \- including global programs, online learning, and on\-the\-job learning.
* Penalty rates and time in lieu for extended field work in remote locations.
* Career development, with opportunities to expand your knowledge across various ecological disciplines, attend conferences and undertake training.
* Flexible work arrangements, including changes to patterns of hours worked, and opportunities to work from home.
* Ability to purchase up to four weeks of additional leave and provision for school term contracts.
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is accessible to employees and their immediate family.
* Social and professional clubs within Stantec to enhance connection, interactions and upskilling across Australia.
* Access to bonus programs within the business.
* Professional Registration and Memberships.
* Salary Continuance Insurance (SCI).
* Service Recognition Awards.
* Employee Referral Benefits.
* Consideration of relocation assistance for an experienced, interstate candidate.

**About us:**


The Stantec community unites over 30,000 employees working in over 450 locations across six continents. We collaborate across disciplines and industries to bring buildings, energy, resources, water, environmental, transport and infrastructure projects to life.


Our work from initial project concept and planning through design, construction, and commissioning begins at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships.


**Culture:**


Stantec is serious about healthy work\-life balance, diversity, inclusion \& equity, indigenous relations, innovation, community engagement, corporate sustainability, and social wellbeing. We have employee groups for women, LGBTQI , neurodiversity, and more! Our employees play sport, fundraise, volunteer, learn, and have fun together.


**How to apply:**


If this position is of interest, please submit your application online.


*Please note that no agency applications will be accepted at this time.*


**Qualifications**


* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology or Hydrogeology

jobs.title: GHD Graduate Program 2026/27 - WA - Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**We’re GHD.**

We don’t do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world’s biggest challenges.


We’re engineers, scientists, designers, architects, planners, advisors, innovators and change makers, committed to making energy, water and communities sustainable for generations to come.


Since 1928, we’ve been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.


**Who could you be at GHD?**

Our **Contamination, Assessment and Remediation** teams are looking for graduates based in WA to join our 2027 Graduate cohort, commencing in **February 2027\.**

Opportunities are available across multiple business groups in our **Perth** offices.


Our two\-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we’ll help you detangle any challenges along the way. You’ll work collaboratively with peers across other disciplines within GHD, as well as with our clients, and connect across the business to share insights, knowledge and improve your overall technical capabilities.


**A frizz\-free application process:**

We want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here’s everything you need to help you prep like a pro:


* **Your CV:** This gives us a snapshot of what you’ve studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
* **A cover letter:** Think of this as your chance to show us where you’d love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
* **Your transcript:** This helps us understand what you’ve been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.

**Your journey to joining GHD:**

Here’s what to expect, step by step:


* **Virtual Assessments:** If you make it through the first stage, you’ll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD Graduate roles.
* **Meet the team:** If you’re successful, you’ll have a face\-to\-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We’ll chat through some *behavioural based questions* to learn more about your skills and experience. It’s also a chance for you to get to know us!
* **Offer:** Congratulations! We’ll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We’re committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. **If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability** and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we’re here to help.  



**Start dates and opportunities**

Most of our full\-time roles kick off in February 2027, though some teams might have earlier start dates in mid\-2026\. Plus, there might also be casual work opportunities throughout your final year of study to give you a head start.  



**Ready to shine?**

If you’ve got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10\-15 minutes. Apply now and take the first step toward an exciting career in consulting.  



**GHD: The Power of Commitment**

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.
  

  

Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back. Our *GHD in the Community* program partners with not\-for\-profit organisations so that we can work on pro\-bono projects, as well as volunteering and fundraising for philanthropic and humanitarian causes. As a business, we also channel some of our profits into the *GHD Foundation* *,* a registered charity that addresses disadvantage and inequality in children accessing STEAM education in the countries where we live and work.


Within GHD, our employee groups and networks help us foster community, find our tribe, and celebrate what makes us unique. These groups play a big part in our global diversity, equity and inclusion strategy, creating spaces for meaningful and safe conversations, connecting with likeminded individuals, and creating a voice to leadership.

Join the Environment Health team at Health Protection NSW for an exciting ongoing opportunity and be part of the team enriching health in millions of ways every day, and play a pivotal role in shaping policies and programs that improve the health of communities across NSW. **About us**  

At Health Protection NSW, our values—collaboration, openness, respect and empowerment—guide everything we do. We foster an environment where people are supported to do their best work and grow their careers.
You’ll be part of a high\-performing, purpose\-driven team that values innovation, curiosity and continuous improvement. We invest in your development and provide opportunities to broaden your experience across complex and impactful policy areas.  

We also recognise the importance of balance, offering flexible working arrangements alongside meaningful, challenging work. While regular office presence is essential, we offer flexible work arrangements to support your needs
Above all, we are committed to building a diverse, inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and supported to thrive.  

To learn more about the Ministry and what benefits we offer, access our Employee Benefits Handbook. **About the role**  

This role sits within the Environmental Health Branch in Health Protection NSW. With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we are enhancing health and wellness while developing your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia.  

As a Regional Aboriginal Environmental Health Project Officer, you will play a central role, working closely with the Manager to support all aspects of high\-level project development and implementation of priority projects, including project planning, monitoring and regular reporting.  

You will be able to work both independently and as part of a remote team to provide senior policy advice and develop public and environmental health policies that deliver strategic initiatives and respond to emerging issues related to Aboriginal communities. This is an excellent opportunity for a highly motivated and skilled individual who thrives on variety, enjoys working across teams, engages well with a variety of stakeholders and wants to contribute to improving environmental health and workforce outcomes for Aboriginal people in NSW.
For more information, please read the full **Role Description.** **What you will be doing**  

On a day\-to\-day basis you will assist with the co\-design, development, management and governance of evidence\-based Aboriginal environmental health policy and programs, including housing, infrastructure, and workforce development. You will work closely with public health units, Aboriginal communities and other stakeholders to address public and environmental health issues to protect the health of Aboriginal communities. This will include ensuring high\-quality evidence\-based project planning, management and evaluation.  

The position will require regular travel to remote communities with overnight stays of up to a week at a time to assist with project delivery. **About you**  

We are seeking a highly motivated, self\-driven and high\-performing public health professional who is committed to making a difference in the health system. You bring excellent understanding and experience in policy, program or project delivery, combined with the ability to navigate complex environments and competing priorities with confidence.  

With tertiary qualifications in environmental health, public health, built environment, and/or relevant work experience in environmental health, you are able to demonstrate an understanding of the range and nature of Aboriginal environmental health issues in NSW. You are self\-motivated, organised, able to work independently as well as part of a remote, dynamic team, and can consult effectively with a variety of stakeholders using high\-level communication and negotiation skills, including superior written, verbal and interpersonal skills. You can effectively use information technology and systems to access and critically interpret literature and apply scientific knowledge and epidemiological methods to the assessment of environmental health risks, particularly in relation to Aboriginal communities. You have a growth mindset, and commitment to continuous learning and personal development. **You will thrive in this role if you:*** Build strong, collaborative relationships and work effectively across teams and stakeholders.
* Are adaptable and comfortable working in a dynamic, fast\-paced environment.
* Are self\-motivated and able to work independently and remotely to achieve team goals.
* Understand (or can quickly build understanding of) government processes and policy frameworks.
* Communicate clearly and influence effectively at all levels.
* Bring a proactive mindset, sound judgement and a commitment to continuous learning and improvement.
* Most importantly, you are motivated by meaningful work and want to contribute to improving outcomes for individuals, families and communities across NSW.

**Description**


We have an exciting opportunity for an **Environmental Scientist** to join our growing **Contaminated Land team** in South Brisbane. As part of our collaborative Contaminated Land Team, you’ll work alongside industry\-leading experts, including Principal and Senior Scientists and Engineers, who are committed to supporting your professional development. At Stantec, you’ll be empowered to shape your own career path with access to tailored development opportunities, ongoing training, and the support needed to achieve your long\-term career goals.


**Day to day tasks would involve:**


* Delivery of preliminary and detailed contaminated land assessments, including site management plans, remediation action plans and high\-quality technical reports.
* Plan and carry out field investigations across soil, vapour, surface water and groundwater, including supervising drilling and sampling programs.
* Work alongside technical specialists and subject matter experts, contributing your insights and learning from others.
* Interpret complex datasets and confidently communicate findings through clear, well\-structured and defensible reporting.
* Play an active role in developing proposals, budgets and tenders, directly contributing to the growth and direction of the team.

**To be successful in the role, you’ll need:**


* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Hydrogeology or Geology.
* 3 years’ minimum experience in the contaminated land industry.
* Exposure to a diverse range of contaminated land investigations across different sites, contaminants and project types.
* Sound soil logging, data management, analytical and technical writing skills, with pride in producing high\-quality work.
* A current driver’s licence and willingness to undertake field work.
* We also have interest in hearing from applicants who have experience in one or several of the following areas (although these are not critical):

» water quality assessment (groundwater, surface water, wastewater, irrigation),


» acid sulphate soils and acid mine drainage,


» landfill assessment and management,


» compliance monitoring/reporting


**This position includes both office and field work, and applicants must be physically able to stand and work in the field.**

Along with a competitive remuneration package commensurate with skills and experience, we offer a number of benefits to ensure ongoing professional development and well\-being:


* Part of a broader Environment and Geoscience Team with support across Australia, and the opportunity to diversify your skill set nationally and globally.

* Penalty rates and time in lieu for extended field work in remote locations.
* Career development, with opportunities to expand your knowledge across various ecological disciplines, attend conferences and undertake training.
* Flexible work arrangements, including changes to patterns of hours worked, and opportunities to work from home.
* Ability to purchase up to four weeks of additional leave and provision for school term contracts.
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is accessible to employees and their immediate family.
* Social and professional clubs within Stantec to enhance connection, interactions and upskilling across Australia.
* Access to bonus programs within the business.
* Professional Registration and Memberships.
* Salary Continuance Insurance (SCI).
* Service Recognition Awards.
* Employee Referral Benefits.
* Consideration of relocation assistance for an experienced, interstate candidate.

The Stantec community unites over 30,000 employees working in over 450 locations across six continents. We collaborate across disciplines and industries to bring buildings, energy, resources, water, environmental, transport and infrastructure projects to life.

new_jobs.description:
**We’re GHD.**

We don’t do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world’s biggest challenges.


We’re engineers, scientists, designers, architects, planners, advisors, innovators and change makers, committed to making energy, water and communities sustainable for generations to come.


Since 1928, we’ve been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.


**Who could you be at GHD?**

Our **Contamination, Assessment and Remediation** teams are looking for graduates based in WA to join our 2027 Graduate cohort, commencing in **February 2027\.**

Opportunities are available across multiple business groups in our **Perth** offices.


Our two\-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we’ll help you detangle any challenges along the way. You’ll work collaboratively with peers across other disciplines within GHD, as well as with our clients, and connect across the business to share insights, knowledge and improve your overall technical capabilities.


**A frizz\-free application process:**

We want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here’s everything you need to help you prep like a pro:


* **Your CV:** This gives us a snapshot of what you’ve studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
* **A cover letter:** Think of this as your chance to show us where you’d love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
* **Your transcript:** This helps us understand what you’ve been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.

**Your journey to joining GHD:**

Here’s what to expect, step by step:


* **Virtual Assessments:** If you make it through the first stage, you’ll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD Graduate roles.
* **Meet the team:** If you’re successful, you’ll have a face\-to\-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We’ll chat through some *behavioural based questions* to learn more about your skills and experience. It’s also a chance for you to get to know us!
* **Offer:** Congratulations! We’ll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We’re committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. **If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability** and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we’re here to help.  



**Start dates and opportunities**

Most of our full\-time roles kick off in February 2027, though some teams might have earlier start dates in mid\-2026\. Plus, there might also be casual work opportunities throughout your final year of study to give you a head start.  



**Ready to shine?**

If you’ve got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10\-15 minutes. Apply now and take the first step toward an exciting career in consulting.  



**GHD: The Power of Commitment**

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.
  

  

Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back. Our *GHD in the Community* program partners with not\-for\-profit organisations so that we can work on pro\-bono projects, as well as volunteering and fundraising for philanthropic and humanitarian causes. As a business, we also channel some of our profits into the *GHD Foundation* *,* a registered charity that addresses disadvantage and inequality in children accessing STEAM education in the countries where we live and work.


Within GHD, our employee groups and networks help us foster community, find our tribe, and celebrate what makes us unique. These groups play a big part in our global diversity, equity and inclusion strategy, creating spaces for meaningful and safe conversations, connecting with likeminded individuals, and creating a voice to leadership.

At Health Protection NSW, our values—collaboration, openness, respect and empowerment—guide everything we do. We foster an environment where people are supported to do their best work and grow their careers.
You’ll be part of a high\-performing, purpose\-driven team that values innovation, curiosity and continuous improvement. We invest in your development and provide opportunities to broaden your experience across complex and impactful policy areas.

This role sits within the Environmental Health Branch in Health Protection NSW. With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we are enhancing health and wellness while developing your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia.  

As a Regional Aboriginal Environmental Health Project Officer, you will play a central role, working closely with the Manager to support all aspects of high\-level project development and implementation of priority projects, including project planning, monitoring and regular reporting.  

You will be able to work both independently and as part of a remote team to provide senior policy advice and develop public and environmental health policies that deliver strategic initiatives and respond to emerging issues related to Aboriginal communities. This is an excellent opportunity for a highly motivated and skilled individual who thrives on variety, enjoys working across teams, engages well with a variety of stakeholders and wants to contribute to improving environmental health and workforce outcomes for Aboriginal people in NSW.
For more information, please read the full **Role Description.** **What you will be doing**  

On a day\-to\-day basis you will assist with the co\-design, development, management and governance of evidence\-based Aboriginal environmental health policy and programs, including housing, infrastructure, and workforce development. You will work closely with public health units, Aboriginal communities and other stakeholders to address public and environmental health issues to protect the health of Aboriginal communities. This will include ensuring high\-quality evidence\-based project planning, management and evaluation.  

The position will require regular travel to remote communities with overnight stays of up to a week at a time to assist with project delivery. **About you**  

We are seeking a highly motivated, self\-driven and high\-performing public health professional who is committed to making a difference in the health system. You bring excellent understanding and experience in policy, program or project delivery, combined with the ability to navigate complex environments and competing priorities with confidence.  

With tertiary qualifications in environmental health, public health, built environment, and/or relevant work experience in environmental health, you are able to demonstrate an understanding of the range and nature of Aboriginal environmental health issues in NSW. You are self\-motivated, organised, able to work independently as well as part of a remote, dynamic team, and can consult effectively with a variety of stakeholders using high\-level communication and negotiation skills, including superior written, verbal and interpersonal skills. You can effectively use information technology and systems to access and critically interpret literature and apply scientific knowledge and epidemiological methods to the assessment of environmental health risks, particularly in relation to Aboriginal communities. You have a growth mindset, and commitment to continuous learning and personal development. **You will thrive in this role if you:*** Build strong, collaborative relationships and work effectively across teams and stakeholders.
* Are adaptable and comfortable working in a dynamic, fast\-paced environment.
* Are self\-motivated and able to work independently and remotely to achieve team goals.
* Understand (or can quickly build understanding of) government processes and policy frameworks.
* Communicate clearly and influence effectively at all levels.
* Bring a proactive mindset, sound judgement and a commitment to continuous learning and improvement.
* Most importantly, you are motivated by meaningful work and want to contribute to improving outcomes for individuals, families and communities across NSW.
